sn11.17:1.2: Now on that occasion the Blessed One had gone for his day’s abiding and was in seclusion.
sn11.17:1.3: Then Sakka, lord of the devas, and Brahma Sahampati approached the Blessed One and stood one at each doorpost.
sn11.17:1.4: Then Sakka, lord of the devas, recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
sn11.17:2.1: “Rise up, O hero, victor in battle! Your burden lowered,
sn11.17:2.2: debt-free one, wander in the world.
sn11.17:2.4: Like the moon on the fifteenth night.”
sn11.17:3.1: Brahma Sahampati: “It is not in such a way that the Tathagatas are to be venerated, lord of the devas.
sn11.17:3.2: The Tathagatas are to be venerated thus:
sn11.17:4.1: “Rise up, O hero, victor in battle! O caravan leader,
sn11.17:4.2: debt-free one, wander in the world.
sn11.17:4.3: Teach the Dhamma, O Blessed One:
sn11.17:4.4: There will be those who will understand.”
